query: Why do some incidents take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: resolution_time_hours
per_column.rationale: This is the target variable for the query -- it directly quantifies how long incidents take, enabling all grouping/modelling. Derivable from opened_at and closed_at, both present. The -1 sentinel (128 rows) is a reasonable 'unresolved/unknown' marker. Values appear consistent with the timestamps, so groundedness is high.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: An original 'priority' column already exists; this appears to be a trivial numeric restatement, adding little new analytical leverage. Values are grounded (a direct read of priority).

per_column.name: category_criticality
per_column.rationale: Mapping category to a criticality tier gives a genuine new axis to compare resolution time against. However the criticality assignment is an inferred judgement not explicitly present; the evidence samples do not even show the source category, so the specific 1/2/3 assignment is only weakly warranted from the text and risks imposed rankings.

per_column.name: is_weekend_opened
per_column.rationale: Weekend-vs-weekday opening is a plausible driver of longer resolution, offering a clean new grouping axis. Derivable from opened_at. One sample flagged 2023-01-02 (a Monday) as weekend=1, which is questionable, suggesting some derivation inaccuracy, but the concept is well grounded.

judge.rationale: The set provides the core target metric (resolution_time_hours) plus two genuinely useful explanatory axes (weekend timing, category criticality) that support the 'why do some take longer' analysis. priority_level is largely redundant with the existing priority column. Most values are soundly derivable from present timestamp/category fields, though category_criticality involves an unshown inferred ranking and at least one weekend flag looks mis-derived, mildly lowering groundedness.
